items.title: Force newest lock file format (revision = 3, upload-time=...)
items.reason: Reports the same mixed-version collaboration problem: older uv releases remove newer lockfile metadata. Its request was to force a format upgrade, rather than prevent downgrades. Maintainers recommended required-version and closed it with guidance to use --refresh.

items.title: Support frozen sync without workspace manifests
items.reason: Introduced the affected manifest-free uv sync --frozen workflow, requiring lockfile revision 5 or later. Released in uv 0.12.23, before the reported 0.13.5; explains the downstream error but does not prevent older writers from downgrading the lockfile.

items.title: Record workspace member default groups in lockfiles
items.reason: Bumped the lockfile to revision 5 to record workspace-member default groups. Released in uv 0.12.22; establishes why losing newer metadata matters for frozen discovery, rather than being only a cosmetic revision change.

items.title: Add `--force` flag to `uv lock` for lockfile format migration
items.reason: Proposed --force to regenerate an older format while retaining package-version preferences. Closed unmerged because --refresh already provides that capability. It did not implement the requested downgrade refusal or an override for that refusal.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues using the exact frozen-discovery error, revision/downgrade/downgrading, revision 5, overwrite, older uv, lockfile format/compatibility, preserve, force, and required-version, including area:lock terminology and searches without platform or version constraints. Searched open, closed, and merged PRs for revision, downgrade, lockfile, and frozen discovery. PR keyword searches returned no hits, so additionally scanned 3,000 recent PR titles across all states and followed historical references. Inspected candidate bodies, comments, relevant reviews, source, and release notes. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#21890 and its linked astral-sh/uv#21864 as downgrade fixes: they concern parsing newer formats and explicitly retain readable newer revisions. Also ruled out astral-sh/uv#16348 (invalid TOML recovery), astral-sh/uv#20646 (whitespace validation), and astral-sh/uv#10988 (marker changes). Followed astral-sh/uv#15220 through astral-sh/uv#15757, astral-sh/uv#19579, and astral-sh/uv#15994; no prior downgrade-prevention fix was found.

type_reason: Rewriting a newer lockfile with an older revision can discard metadata needed by manifest-free frozen sync, breaking a previously usable lockfile. Historical revision-3 writer code and current source support this mechanism; accepting newer revisions for reading does not protect them when rewriting. The requested refusal and override need design, but the reported metadata loss is a correctness problem. The related format-upgrade request does not track downgrade prevention, and no previously fixed downgrade guard was found.
summary: astral-sh/uv#15220 is the closest historical discussion of mixed-version metadata loss. astral-sh/uv#22010 and astral-sh/uv#22018 establish the revision-5 requirement behind the failure; astral-sh/uv#19579 shows that the earlier --force proposal was closed unmerged. No matching downgrade-prevention fix was found.
draft_response:
The downgrade can remove metadata needed by frozen sync. The quoted error specifically comes from discovering uv.lock without the workspace’s pyproject.toml, which requires revision 5 or later (astral-sh/uv#22018). The related discussion in astral-sh/uv#15220 covers upgrading the format, but does not provide a downgrade guard.

For now, set `required-version = ">=0.12.23"` under `[tool.uv]` in pyproject.toml to reject older writers, and regenerate with `uv lock --refresh` using a compatible uv version while the workspace manifest is present. Please share the exact older uv version and command that rewrote the file; 0.13.5 alone does not identify the writer. Any write guard needs to preserve support for reading compatible newer revisions.
